calls.reason: MIT's 2022 arithmetic tests and Qian's symbolic tests show GPT-3 failing equivalent formats and unfamiliar instances. Assisted successes qualify the claim but do not overturn its contemporary point about incomplete generalization.
OpenAI acknowledges plausible errors, while HELM shows substantial factual competence. Neither directly establishes how reliably GPT distinguishes appropriate entity-property combinations.

The pastiche description is rhetorical. TruthfulQA links some falsehoods to imitated misconceptions, but neither it nor OpenAI's training account establishes the cause of novel churro-surgery combinations.
ROME identifies mechanisms for factual associations in other models, but does not test whether embedding-driven substitutions cause GPT-3's useful paraphrases and recurring mistakes.

OpenAI documents training on human demonstrations, and McCoy finds novel GPT-2 constructions. Neither establishes whether every plausible fragment derives from human utterances or why the combinations sound plausible.

Kim and Schuster show GPT-3 tracking failures during inference; Chang shows training-related forgetting in OLMo. Together they suggest a possibility but do not establish that GPT-3 loses entity-property associations during training.
